domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers basic microbiology, infection control procedures, safety data sheets, human physiology, skin histology, skin disorders, and basic chemistry related to cosmetic ingredients and pH levels for professional estheticians.

This section evaluates client consultation, skin analysis, contraindications, cleansing, steaming, exfoliation, massage movements, extractions, mask applications, facial service conclusions, electrical equipment, and makeup principles used during daily professional skin care practice.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive at the testing center with your valid picture ID. Cellular phones, watches, electronic devices, printed materials, and notes are strictly prohibited in the testing area. Follow all proctor instructions closely to ensure a smooth testing experience and maintain the integrity of the exam.

faq.answer_text: The examination is comprised of 110 items in total. These items are designed to evaluate your theoretical knowledge across the two primary domains of scientific concepts and skin care services to ensure you meet the standards for professional licensure.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: The total time allowed for the esthetics theory examination is 90 minutes. Candidates should manage their time effectively to ensure they complete all sections of the test within this designated period to achieve a passing result.

The examination is developed by the National-Interstate Council of State Boards of Cosmetology. It serves as the standard licensure assessment for estheticians to verify their theoretical knowledge before they begin working in a professional capacity.

If you are looking for information regarding the current certification path or potential updates to the testing requirements, please check with National-Interstate Council of State Boards of Cosmetology (NIC) for the current certification path.

editorial.overview: The NIC Esthetics Theory State Board Examination serves as the primary licensure test for aspiring estheticians, developed by the National-Interstate Council of State Boards of Cosmetology. This 90-minute assessment features 110 items across two distinct domains, evaluating core scientific concepts and practical skin care services required for safe, professional practice in the industry. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in these areas to meet the standards set by state boards for licensure and entry into the field of professional skin care.
editorial.preparation_strategy: To prepare effectively, review the candidate information bulletin and study approved reference textbooks. Focus your study efforts on the core domains of scientific concepts and skin care services to ensure you are ready for the 110 items on the test. Consistent review of these materials will help you master the concepts required for the examination and achieve a passing score.
editorial.who_should_take: Candidates pursuing professional licensure as estheticians must take this examination. It is required by state boards of cosmetology to verify theoretical knowledge before individuals are permitted to enter professional practice and provide services to the public.
